request.prompt:
Job T08: usp_fraud_flags (tsql), legacy file estate/tsql/T08_usp_fraud_flags.sql (SHA-256 6e90a4a5ad66f2169982f70407d488edd7b7e0053a0617f71b9e9947cb9de886).
Rule-based fraud indicators for recently notified claims.
Invocations, in order: run: AsOfDate=2025-12-31.

Legacy code:
/*==============================================================================
  Job       rpt.usp_fraud_flags
  Purpose   Fraud indicators for the Special Investigations Unit (SIU): one row
            per claim notified in the twelve months to the reporting date, with
            the indicator flags, a score and a referral band for the SIU
            worklist and case tool.
  Author    MOB
  Run by    SIU_WEEKLY, after the claims and policy extracts and dw.dim_customer
            have loaded
  Output    rpt.claim_fraud_flags (full refresh)

  Change log
    2016-05-09  MOB   Initial version: early notification and new customer
                      indicators (CR-0954)
    2016-11-21  MOB   Motor claims: registration not in the Irish format
                      (CR-1012)
    2017-04-03  SB    Claim keyed against a policy from another line of
                      business (INC-1530)
    2018-08-27  SB    fraud_score and referral bands agreed with SIU (CR-1377)
    2019-02-11  NF    Policy dates from the latest policy extract on or before
                      the reporting date, not the old policy master (CR-1529)
    2020-06-15  NF    loss_day_key and reason text for the SIU case tool
                      (CR-1810)
    2021-10-04  SB    lob_code upper-cased for the SIU dashboard (INC-2389)
==============================================================================*/
SET NOCOUNT ON;
GO
IF OBJECT_ID(N'rpt.claim_fraud_flags', N'U') IS NULL
CREATE TABLE rpt.claim_fraud_flags (
    claim_id                 INT            NOT NULL,
    claim_number             VARCHAR(20)    NOT NULL,
    policy_id                INT            NOT NULL,
    policy_number            VARCHAR(20)    NULL,
    customer_id              INT            NOT NULL,
    lob_code                 VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
    loss_date                DATE           NOT NULL,
    reported_date            DATE           NOT NULL,
    early_notification_flag  INT            NOT NULL,
    invalid_reg_flag         INT            NOT NULL,
    new_customer_flag        INT            NOT NULL,
    lob_mismatch_flag        INT            NOT NULL,
    fraud_score              INT            NOT NULL,
    fraud_band               VARCHAR(6)     NOT NULL,  -- HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW
    loss_day_key             CHAR(8)        NOT NULL,  -- yyyymmdd, day key in the case tool
    reason_text              VARCHAR(100)   NOT NULL,
    as_of_date               DATE           NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_rpt_claim_fraud_flags PRIMARY KEY (claim_id)
);
GO
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE rpt.usp_fraud_flags
    @AsOfDate DATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    DECLARE @job_name       VARCHAR(128) = 'rpt.usp_fraud_flags',
            @rows           INT,
            @snapshot_date  DATE,
            @err_msg        NVARCHAR(4000),
            @err_no         INT;

    BEGIN TRY
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';

        /* Policy details from the latest policy extract on or before the reporting date */
        SELECT  @snapshot_date = MAX(ps.snapshot_date)
        FROM    stg.policy_snapshots ps WITH (NOLOCK)
        WHERE   ps.snapshot_date <= @AsOfDate;

        /* 1. Claims notified in the twelve months to the reporting date, with the
              policy they were made under and when the policyholder became a customer */
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#claims') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #claims;

        SELECT  c.claim_id,
                c.claim_number,
                c.policy_id,
                c.customer_id,
                c.lob_code,
                c.loss_date,
                c.reported_date,
                p.policy_number,
                p.inception_date,
                p.expiry_date,
                p.vehicle_reg,
                dc.customer_since
        INTO    #claims
        FROM    stg.claims c WITH (NOLOCK)
        LEFT JOIN stg.policy_snapshots p WITH (NOLOCK)
               ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id
              AND p.snapshot_date = @snapshot_date
        LEFT JOIN dw.dim_customer dc WITH (NOLOCK)
               ON dc.customer_id = c.customer_id
        WHERE   c.reported_date >  DATEADD(MONTH, -12, @AsOfDate)
          AND   c.reported_date <= @AsOfDate;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'claims notified', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        /* 2. SIU indicators, one point each (CR-0954, CR-1012, INC-1530) */
        IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#flags') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #flags;

        SELECT  f.*,
                f.early_notification_flag + f.invalid_reg_flag
                  + f.new_customer_flag + f.lob_mismatch_flag     AS fraud_score
        INTO    #flags
        FROM   (SELECT  cl.claim_id,
                        -- claim notified within 30 days of the cover starting
                        CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(DAY, cl.expiry_date, cl.reported_date) BETWEEN 0 AND 30
                             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                    AS early_notification_flag,
                        -- motor: registration not in the Irish format, e.g. 191-D-12345
                        CASE WHEN cl.lob_code = 'MOT'
                              AND cl.vehicle_reg NOT LIKE '[0-9][0-9]%-[A-Z]%-[0-9]%'
                             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                    AS invalid_reg_flag,
                        -- customer for less than six months at the date of loss
                        CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(DAY, cl.customer_since, cl.loss_date) < 180
                             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                    AS new_customer_flag,
                        -- policy number starts with its line of business (MOT/2024/500001)
                        CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(cl.policy_number, 0, 4) <> cl.lob_code
                             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                    AS lob_mismatch_flag
                FROM    #claims cl) f;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'indicators', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;

        /* 3. Reload the SIU table: bands agreed with SIU (CR-1377) */
        BEGIN TRANSACTION;

        TRUNCATE TABLE rpt.claim_fraud_flags;

        INSERT INTO rpt.claim_fraud_flags
               (claim_id, claim_number, policy_id, policy_number, customer_id, lob_code,
                loss_date, reported_date, early_notification_flag, invalid_reg_flag,
                new_customer_flag, lob_mismatch_flag, fraud_score, fraud_band,
                loss_day_key, reason_text, as_of_date)
        SELECT  cl.claim_id,
                cl.claim_number,
                cl.policy_id,
                cl.policy_number,
                cl.customer_id,
                UPPER(RTRIM(cl.lob_code)),
                cl.loss_date,
                cl.reported_date,
                f.early_notification_flag,
                f.invalid_reg_flag,
                f.new_customer_flag,
                f.lob_mismatch_flag,
                f.fraud_score,
                CASE WHEN f.fraud_score >= 2 THEN 'HIGH'
                     WHEN f.fraud_score = 1  THEN 'MEDIUM'
                     ELSE 'LOW'
                END,
                CONVERT(CHAR(8), cl.loss_date, 112),
                'Notified ' + CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), cl.reported_date, 103)
                    + CASE WHEN f.fraud_score = 0 THEN ' - no indicators' ELSE ' -' END
                    + CASE WHEN f.early_notification_flag = 1 THEN ' EARLY'   ELSE '' END
                    + CASE WHEN f.invalid_reg_flag        = 1 THEN ' REG'     ELSE '' END
                    + CASE WHEN f.new_customer_flag       = 1 THEN ' NEWCUST' ELSE '' END
                    + CASE WHEN f.lob_mismatch_flag       = 1 THEN ' LOB'     ELSE '' END,
                @AsOfDate
        FROM    #claims cl
        JOIN    #flags f
                ON f.claim_id = cl.claim_id;

        SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;

        COMMIT TRANSACTION;

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'rpt.claim_fraud_flags', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;

        SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
                @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();

        EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
             @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
        THROW;
    END CATCH
END;
GO

request.system_prompt:
Translate one legacy T-SQL (SQL Server 2022) job to PySpark 4.2. Your output must reproduce the legacy output EXACTLY, record for record and value for value, bugs included: reconciliation compares every row and column with the legacy engine's own output.

Write one Python module:
- Imports only from pyspark (pyspark.sql, pyspark.sql.functions as F, pyspark.sql.types as T, pyspark.sql.Window), datetime, decimal, math, re, functools and typing.
- Exactly this entry point: def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
- inputs holds every input table by its legacy name in lower case (e.g. "stg.claims"); params holds the parameters as text (e.g. params["AsOfDate"] == "2025-12-31").
- Return a dict from each output's legacy name to a DataFrame with the output's columns. The harness then casts each column to the contract type shown, as the legacy table's insert would (so a decimal(38,6) value stored into decimal(14,2) is rounded half up).
- Never do I/O or reach engine internals: no spark.read, .write, saveAsTable, spark.conf, RDDs, UDFs, .cache(), getattr, eval, open, os or sys. spark.sql, F.expr and selectExpr only with plain string literals (no f-strings).
- Use only constants that appear in the legacy code, the parameters, or a trap card's fix guidance (format patterns, collation names). Never hard-code data values.
- Reproduce every legacy behaviour exactly, including anything that looks like a bug: never fix it. Mark each line that reproduces a suspected bug with a "# LANSH-DEFECT: <what>" comment and list the bug in defects.
- Row order: Spark has none. Wherever the result depends on order (first or last row, a running value, a cursor, NODUPKEY, RETAIN, LAG), sort on the legacy ORDER BY and then _row_seq, which every source table has in its original row order.
- Spark runs with ANSI mode on: overflow and invalid casts raise errors, and a division by zero raises; use try_divide or a guard only where the legacy engine returns NULL.

structured_output.code:
"""Job T08: rpt.usp_fraud_flags (legacy T-SQL, estate/tsql/T08_usp_fraud_flags.sql).

Fraud indicators for the SIU: one row for each claim notified in the twelve
months to the reporting date, with indicator flags, a score, a referral band, a
yyyymmdd loss day key and reason text. Output: rpt.claim_fraud_flags (full refresh).

Legacy bugs are reproduced on purpose and marked with '# LANSH-DEFECT'.
"""
import datetime

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, SparkSession
import pyspark.sql.functions as F


def _ci(col):
    # SQL Server default collation (CI, trailing-space-insensitive) for '=' / '<>'
    return F.upper(F.rtrim(col))


def run(spark: SparkSession, inputs: dict[str, DataFrame], params: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, DataFrame]:
    as_of = F.lit(datetime.date.fromisoformat(params["AsOfDate"]))

    claims_src = inputs["stg.claims"]
    ps = inputs["stg.policy_snapshots"]
    dc = inputs["dw.dim_customer"]

    # @snapshot_date = MAX(snapshot_date) WHERE snapshot_date <= @AsOfDate (NULL -> no policy matches)
    snap = ps.filter(F.col("snapshot_date") <= as_of).agg(F.max("snapshot_date").alias("snap_max"))
    pol = (
        ps.join(snap, ps["snapshot_date"] == snap["snap_max"], "inner")
        .select(
            F.col("policy_id").alias("p_policy_id"),
            F.col("policy_number"),
            F.col("inception_date"),
            F.col("expiry_date"),
            F.col("vehicle_reg"),
        )
    )
    cust = dc.select(F.col("customer_id").alias("dc_customer_id"), F.col("customer_since"))

    # 1. #claims
    c = claims_src.filter(
        (F.col("reported_date") > F.add_months(as_of, -12)) & (F.col("reported_date") <= as_of)
    )
    cl = (
        c.join(pol, c["policy_id"] == pol["p_policy_id"], "left")
        .join(cust, c["customer_id"] == cust["dc_customer_id"], "left")
        .select(
            c["claim_id"], c["claim_number"], c["policy_id"], c["customer_id"], c["lob_code"],
            c["loss_date"], c["reported_date"],
            pol["policy_number"], pol["inception_date"], pol["expiry_date"], pol["vehicle_reg"],
            cust["customer_since"],
        )
    )

    # 2. #flags
    days_exp_to_rep = F.datediff(F.col("reported_date"), F.col("expiry_date"))
    # LANSH-DEFECT: measures from expiry_date, not inception_date (cover start)
    early = F.when((days_exp_to_rep >= 0) & (days_exp_to_rep <= 30), F.lit(1)).otherwise(F.lit(0))

    # vehicle_reg NOT LIKE '[0-9][0-9]%-[A-Z]%-[0-9]%' (case-insensitive collation; NULL -> unknown -> 0)
    reg_like = F.col("vehicle_reg").rlike("(?s)^[0-9][0-9].*-[A-Za-z].*-[0-9]")
    invalid_reg = F.when(
        (_ci(F.col("lob_code")) == F.lit("MOT")) & (~reg_like), F.lit(1)
    ).otherwise(F.lit(0))

    new_cust = F.when(
        F.datediff(F.col("loss_date"), F.col("customer_since")) < 180, F.lit(1)
    ).otherwise(F.lit(0))

    # T-SQL SUBSTRING(policy_number, 0, 4) returns only characters 1..3
    pol_prefix = F.substring(F.col("policy_number"), 1, 3)  # LANSH-DEFECT: SUBSTRING(...,0,4) yields 3 chars, so lob codes longer than 3 chars always mismatch
    lob_mismatch = F.when(_ci(pol_prefix) != _ci(F.col("lob_code")), F.lit(1)).otherwise(F.lit(0))

    f = cl.select(
        F.col("claim_id").alias("f_claim_id"),
        early.alias("early_notification_flag"),
        invalid_reg.alias("invalid_reg_flag"),
        new_cust.alias("new_customer_flag"),
        lob_mismatch.alias("lob_mismatch_flag"),
    ).withColumn(
        "fraud_score",
        F.col("early_notification_flag") + F.col("invalid_reg_flag")
        + F.col("new_customer_flag") + F.col("lob_mismatch_flag"),
    )

    # 3. Insert: #claims JOIN #flags ON claim_id
    j = cl.join(f, cl["claim_id"] == f["f_claim_id"], "inner")

    score = F.col("fraud_score")
    band = (
        F.when(score >= 2, F.lit("HIGH"))
        .when(score == 1, F.lit("MEDIUM"))
        .otherwise(F.lit("LOW"))
    )
    reason = F.concat(
        F.lit("Notified "),
        F.date_format(F.col("reported_date"), "dd/MM/yyyy"),
        F.when(score == 0, F.lit(" - no indicators")).otherwise(F.lit(" -")),
        F.when(F.col("early_notification_flag") == 1, F.lit(" EARLY")).otherwise(F.lit("")),
        F.when(F.col("invalid_reg_flag") == 1, F.lit(" REG")).otherwise(F.lit("")),
        F.when(F.col("new_customer_flag") == 1, F.lit(" NEWCUST")).otherwise(F.lit("")),
        F.when(F.col("lob_mismatch_flag") == 1, F.lit(" LOB")).otherwise(F.lit("")),
    )

    out = j.select(
        F.col("claim_id"),
        F.col("claim_number"),
        F.col("policy_id"),
        F.col("policy_number"),
        F.col("customer_id"),
        F.upper(F.rtrim(F.col("lob_code"))).alias("lob_code"),
        F.col("loss_date"),
        F.col("reported_date"),
        F.col("early_notification_flag"),
        F.col("invalid_reg_flag"),
        F.col("new_customer_flag"),
        F.col("lob_mismatch_flag"),
        F.col("fraud_score"),
        band.alias("fraud_band"),
        F.date_format(F.col("loss_date"), "yyyyMMdd").alias("loss_day_key"),
        reason.alias("reason_text"),
        as_of.alias("as_of_date"),
    )

    return {"rpt.claim_fraud_flags": out}

defects.intended: Flag claims notified within 30 days of the cover starting, so it should use DATEDIFF(DAY, inception_date, reported_date).
defects.title: Early notification measured from policy expiry instead of inception
defects.what_it_does: Sets the flag when DATEDIFF(DAY, expiry_date, reported_date) is between 0 and 30, which means the claim was notified in the 30 days after the cover ended.

defects.intended: Compare the policy-number prefix (the part before the first '/') with the full lob_code.
defects.title: SUBSTRING(policy_number, 0, 4) returns only 3 characters
defects.what_it_does: Because T-SQL starts counting at position 0, SUBSTRING(policy_number, 0, 4) returns only the first 3 characters. Any lob_code longer than 3 characters therefore never matches, and its claims always get lob_mismatch_flag = 1.

structured_output.notes:
I didn't get any trap cards for this job, so traps_handled is empty. The code hasn't been run against data yet; please check these points:
1. Collation: I assumed the default case-insensitive, accent-sensitive SQL Server collation. So lob_code = 'MOT' and SUBSTRING(...) <> lob_code are compared after UPPER(RTRIM()) on both sides. The LIKE class [A-Z] is written as [A-Za-z]. Under a SQL_Latin1 collation, the [A-Z] range in a LIKE pattern can also match accented letters; my regex doesn't, so this needs checking if registrations contain such characters.
2. The LIKE pattern is written as the Java regex (?s)^[0-9][0-9].*-[A-Za-z].*-[0-9]. A NULL vehicle_reg gives NOT LIKE = unknown, so the flag is 0. A NULL policy_number gives <> = unknown, so the flag is 0.
3. In Spark, substring(x, 0, 4) would return 4 characters, so the code uses substring(x, 1, 3) to match what T-SQL returns.
4. If no snapshot exists on or before AsOfDate, @snapshot_date is NULL and every policy column comes back NULL. An inner join to the MAX value reproduces this.
5. Joins are reproduced as written. #claims JOIN #flags is a real join on claim_id, so duplicate snapshot, customer or claim rows multiply the same way they do in the legacy job. In the legacy job they would also break the primary key and fail the job.
6. DATEADD(MONTH, -12) maps to add_months; both clamp to the end of the month.
7. Date formats: style 112 is written as yyyyMMdd and style 103 as dd/MM/yyyy.
